news.title: Shared API keys expose AI agents at 69% of enterprises, new VentureBeat research finds
news.summary_raw: Share one API key across five AI agents, and a single compromised agent inherits the reach of all five. The attacker immediately benefits from the accumulated permissions of every workflow that the key touches. The forensic trail goes cold at the credential level because five agents on one account leave no record of which agent did what.Sixty-nine percent of enterprises run agents with credential sharing somewhere in their deployments, according to VentureBeat’s June 2026 Pulse Research wave of
news.summary: VentureBeat research revealed that 69% of enterprises expose AI agents to API key sharing, putting multiple AI instances under a single compromised key's control. This makes it challenging to detect the root cause of attacks, as forensic trails are erased by shared credentials.
news.enterprise_use: Review your API key management practices in your AWS, Azure, Okta, or SSO providers, as 69% of similar enterprises use shared API keys between multiple AI agents. Enable strict credential isolation and consider using AI-specific endpoint security tools, such as CrowdStrike, to monitor for suspicious activity.
